Priya (CS): Hey team — customer AcmeFabrics (acct 0xA1B2C3) says their trial credits dropped to 0 in the middle of a scheduled load test. They were actively sending requests when auth started failing with 403s. Can we extend or reinstate?

Alex (CS Ops): Timeline from customer: started ramp at ~2026-06-08T09:10Z, calls succeeded until ~2026-06-08T09:47Z, after that they got rapid 403s. They attached logs. I looked — promo credits show expired at 2026-06-08T09:45Z UTC.

Priya (CS): They claim they received an email earlier in their timezone saying expiry was end-of-day local, so they expected a few more hours.

Tomas (Billing): Billing view: promo grant id PG-77821 applied 2026-05-09, TTL = 30 days, auto-expired at UTC timestamp above. No manual override recorded.

Sophie (Support Manager): Policy reminder — standard trial credits are timeboxed, but we do discretionary 7-day extensions for clear platform-side failures. Do we have evidence of platform error vs timezone/communication mismatch?

Eli (QA): I pulled runtime traces for that window. No service outage or deploys at 09:40-09:50Z. Rate-limiter shows normal behavior. However, there is a corner case: if a promo grant has a local-date expiry field and we convert to UTC incorrectly for recipients in non-UTC zones, the UI email could show different expiry.

Priya (CS): Customer is in CET (UTC+2). They received an email at 2026-06-07 23:58 CET saying "expires tomorrow" (ambiguous). They started heavy tests next morning. They insist we miscommunicated.

Alex (CS Ops): Attach from customer: ``account: 0xA1B2C3
log snippet: "POST /v1/complete 200" until 09:47:21Z then multiple "403 unauthorized - credits exhausted"``

BillingBot: Automated note — Promo PG-77821 reached expiry condition at 2026-06-08T09:45:00Z UTC. No auto-renew configured.

Tomas (Billing): Given logs and no systemic outage, policy technically denies automatic reinstatement beyond TTL. But it's borderline because of the email wording and timezone confusion. I can approve a one-time 72-hour extension if Support Manager signs off. Requires a manual grant transaction so the accounting team has an audit trail.

Sophie (Support Manager): @Tomas please go ahead with the 72-hour discretionary extension. Priya, offer the customer a temporary credit package for their rerun and apologise for the confusion. Also offer to walk them through best-practice for long-running load tests (suggested: dedicated reserved capacity or prebooked promo extension). :handshake:

Priya (CS): On it. I'll DM them the temporary credits and schedule a quick call for onboarding tips. Will confirm once Billing posts the grant.

Tomas (Billing): Grant posted: TX-992311, amount=USD-equivalent trial credit 150. Expires 2026-06-11T09:45:00Z UTC (72h extension). Internal note: discretionary grant, reason = timezone/email ambiguity during active load test.

Priya (CS): Thanks — customer accepted, re-ran tests, no further 403s. They've asked we clarify expiry in future emails.

Eli (QA): I'll file a small tickets item to check email template wording for local-date vs UTC and add a unit test for timezone formatting in promo notifications.

Sophie (Support Manager): Nice work. Keep this thread updated if any downstream billing reconciliation issues pop up.

Priya (CS): Will do. Closing loop now. :white_check_mark:
